channel.title: The Wicked Blog
channel.description: Ideas from the books, argued in public. No fluff, no guru voice.

item.title: Your CRM Is a Database of Market Failures (Start Using It Like One)
item.dc:creator: Michael Gardner
item.description: Your sales team isn't a mechanism for forcing money out of reluctant prospects. It's a sonar array — and you're throwing away everything it pings back.

item.title: When a Kid Says "I Can't Do It"
item.dc:creator: Michael Gardner
item.description: It's almost never about the thing they're looking at. It's about the size of it — and size is the one part you can actually fix.

item.title: Why Motivation Follows Action (Not the Other Way Around)
item.dc:creator: Michael Gardner
item.description: You're waiting to feel like it. You're going to be waiting forever — because the feeling shows up AFTER you start, not before.

item.title: The Four Ways to Fund a Business — and What Each One Does to Your Head
item.dc:creator: Michael Gardner
item.description: Bootstrapping, borrowing, investors, or customers — where the money comes from changes what you build AND who you become while building it.

item.title: How Algorithms Decide What You See (and What That's Costing You)
item.dc:creator: Michael Gardner
item.description: Your feed isn't a window into the world. It's a mirror maze built by a machine whose only job is keeping you inside it.

item.title: The 50 True Fans Math: Why You Don't Need to Go Viral
item.dc:creator: Michael Gardner
item.description: You don't need a million followers. You need fifty people who genuinely want what you make. Here's the arithmetic nobody shows you.

item.title: Teaching Kids About Money Without Making It Weird
item.dc:creator: Michael Gardner
item.description: Kids learn money habits by age seven — mostly by watching you. Here's how to make the lessons stick without a single lecture.

item.title: Nobody Gets the High Horse: What My Dog Taught Me About Judgment
item.dc:creator: Michael Gardner
item.description: My dog Frankie has never once judged another dog. Humans can't get through breakfast without judging somebody. That gap is the whole story.
